name: MirrorCode
description: A long-horizon coding benchmark that evaluates AI agents' ability to autonomously reimplement existing CLI programs without access to source code. Agents receive only execute-only access to reference programs and visible test cases, requiring complete architectural reimplementation across C, Python, and Rust. Target programs range from simple Unix utilities (~1,000 LoC) to full programming language interpreters (~61,000 LoC).
typical_sota_score: Claude Opus 4.6: 100% on choose/cal, 99.95% on gotree (16k LoC), 35% on Pkl (61k LoC); smaller programs largely solved, largest task unsolved
reputation: Early-stage benchmark from a high-credibility Epoch AI and METR collaboration; preliminary results released April 2026 with full release forthcoming.
notes: Contamination risk: models likely encountered source code during training; memorization screens applied but not fully eliminative. Tasks require precise executable specifications uncommon in real development. Domain coverage is selective (excludes networking, graphics, databases, OS-level code). Maximum inference budget ~1B tokens per task (~$550). Only 4 of 24 programs analyzed in preliminary release. Human baseline for gotree reimplementation estimated at 2–17 weeks for skilled engineers.
